chapterNote: The psalm of the majestic Name and the mystery of man. It is framed by one repeated exclamation — O LORD our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth — and everything between the frames measures the distance from glory to dust and back. God's strength is founded, of all places, in the mouths of nursing infants, praise so weak it silences the avenger; and when David walks out under the night sky and considers the moon and stars as mere finger-work, the question every human being has asked under those stars breaks out of him: what is frail man, that You remember him? The answer is more staggering than the question: crowned with glory and honor, a little lower than the heavenly beings, set as ruler over the works of Your hands with everything under his feet — Eden's dominion charter set to music. The New Testament reads the psalm twice over: Jesus claimed verse 2 for the children shouting Hosanna in the temple (Matthew 21:16), and Hebrews 2 reads the whole arc — made lower, then crowned — as the map of Christ Himself, the true Son of Man in whom fallen man's forfeited crown is recovered.

1.text: For the choir director, on the Gittith. A psalm of David. O LORD our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth, You who have set Your glory above the heavens!
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach] upon Gittith [gittith — the instrument or tune of Gath], A Psalm [mizmor] of David. O LORD [YHWH] our Lord [Adon — Sovereign, Master], how excellent [addir — majestic, mighty] is Your name [shem] in all the earth [eretz]! who has set [natan] Your glory [hod — splendor] above the heavens [shamayim].
1.notes: Two names open the psalm: YHWH (H3068), the covenant name, and Adon (H113), the Sovereign — OUR Lord, the covenant people speaking. addir (H117) is majesty with might in it, and the hod (H1935) outruns creation's ceiling: His glory is not IN the heavens but above them.

2.text: Out of the mouths of babes and nursing infants You have founded a stronghold, because of Your adversaries, to silence the enemy and the avenger.
2.amp: Out of the mouth [peh] of babes [olel] and sucklings [yanaq — nursing infants] have You ordained ['founded', yasad, the KJV margin] strength [oz], because of Your enemies [tsarar], that You might still [shabat — make cease] the enemy [oyeb] and the avenger [naqam].
2.notes: yasad (H3245) is foundation-laying: God builds His fortress of oz (H5797) out of the weakest sound the race makes, a nursing child's praise. The war-logic is deliberate — omnipotence silences (shabat, H7673) its enemies with lullabies, and Jesus cited exactly this against the priests as children shouted in the temple (cf. Matthew 21:16).

3.text: When I look up at Your heavens, the work of Your fingers, the moon and the stars that You have set firmly in place,
3.amp: When I consider [raah] Your heavens [shamayim], the work [maaseh] of Your fingers [etsba], the moon [yareach] and the stars [kokab], which You have ordained [kun — established, fixed firm];
3.notes: A night psalm: sun unmentioned, the yareach and kokabim (H3394, H3556) overhead. 'Fingers' (etsba, H676), not even arm or hand — the galaxies as fine-work, embroidery-scale effort for God. kun (H3559): each star fixed in its setting like a stone by a jeweler.

4.text: what is frail man, that You remember him, or the son of Adam, that You attend to him with care?
4.amp: What is man [enosh — frail, mortal man], that You are mindful [zakar — remember] of him? and the son [ben] of man [adam], that You visit [paqad — attend to, care for] him?
4.notes: The question chooses its words for smallness: enosh (H582), man in his frailty, and ben-adam, son of the dust-made one. zakar and paqad (H2142, H6485): not bare awareness but active remembering and visiting care. Under the fixed stars, the astonishment is not that God exists but that He attends.

5.text: Yet You have made him only a little lower than the heavenly beings, and You have crowned him with glory and honor.
5.amp: For You have made him a little [meat] lower [chaser — to lack] than the angels [elohim — the heavenly beings], and have crowned [atar] him with glory [kabod] and honour [hadar — majesty].
5.notes: The answer flies past all expectation: man lacks (chaser, H2637) only a little of elohim (H430) — the heavenly court — and wears kabod and hadar (H3519, H1926), the vocabulary elsewhere reserved for God's own splendor. atar (H5849), crowned: royalty, not accident. Hebrews reads the 'little lower' of Christ's incarnation and the crown of His exaltation (cf. Hebrews 2:7-9).

6.text: You made him ruler over the works of Your hands; You have put everything under his feet:
6.amp: You made him to have dominion [mashal — rule, govern] over the works [maaseh] of Your hands; You have put [shith] all things under his feet [regel]:
6.notes: The Eden charter set to music (cf. Genesis 1:26-28): mashal (H4910) over the maaseh of God's own hands — creation handed to a steward. 'Under his feet' became the New Testament's phrase for Christ's total lordship (cf. 1 Corinthians 15:27; Ephesians 1:22): what Adam fumbled, the Son of Man holds.

7.text: all sheep and oxen, and the beasts of the open field as well,
7.amp: All sheep [tsoneh] and oxen [aleph], yea, and the beasts [behemah] of the field [sadeh]; ['Flocks and oxen all of them', the KJV margin]
7.notes: The inventory begins with the tamed — flock and plow-team, the animals of covenant economy — then steps past the fence to the behemah (H929) of the open sadeh (H7704): dominion running beyond what man has domesticated.

8.text: the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea, and whatever travels the paths of the seas.
8.amp: The fowl [tsippor] of the air [shamayim], and the fish [dag] of the sea [yam], and whatsoever passes through [abar] the paths [orach] of the seas.
8.notes: The three kingdoms of Genesis 1 complete the writ: air, sea, and the mysterious last clause — whatever abar (H5674) the orach yam (H734, H3220), the sea-paths, creatures man had never seen in waters he could not chart. The dominion deed covers territory the steward hasn't visited.

9.text: O LORD our Lord, how majestic Your name is through all the earth!
9.amp: O LORD [YHWH] our Lord [Adon], how excellent [addir — majestic] is Your name [shem] in all the earth [eretz]!
9.notes: The frame closes exactly as it opened — but the singer has been to the stars and back since verse 1, and the refrain returns enriched: the majesty of the Name now includes what He has done with dust. The psalm about man ends, as man himself must, in praise of Someone else.
